walkthroughs.body_html:
Modern Analytical Techniques — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Modern Analytical Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Modern Analytical Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: 0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotope”?
options: Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionisation energy”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electron configuration”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number Z”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number A”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
